evidence.text: Angel Island Ferry Schedule (Tiburon terminal): the 09:05 departure to Ayala Cove is confirmed for 2026-10-09, with 42 of 90 seats still available and an accessible boarding ramp in service. Round-trip fare is $120.00 for a party of two. The dock office notes that bicycle racks are limited to twelve bikes per sailing and that the 09:05 sailing is the last direct crossing before the 11:15 connector, which adds a 40-minute layover at Pier 41. [Page footer, repeated on every fetch of this status endpoint] Angel Island State Park is managed by California State Parks in partnership with the Angel Island Conservancy. General park regulations: quiet hours are 10pm to 6am; all food must be stored in provided bear-resistant lockers; campfires are permitted only in designated steel fire rings and are subject to daily red-flag-warning suspension; pets are not permitted on any island trail or campsite year-round, not only during nesting season; drones require a separate special-use permit obtained at least two weeks in advance; all overnight visitors must check in at the Ayala Cove ranger kiosk before 4pm on arrival day or the reservation may be released. Accessibility statement: California State Parks is committed to providing accessible facilities under the ADA and the California Government Code. Accessible campsites include a hardened, level tent pad reachable without stairs, an adjacent accessible vault toilet or restroom within park guidelines, and a route from the nearest ferry dock or drop-off point with a running slope no steeper than 1:12 for the majority of the route where terrain allows; some historic trail segments retain steeper grades and are flagged individually on each site listing. Visitors requiring further accommodation should contact the park accessibility coordinator at least 72 hours before arrival. Ferry general terms and conditions: fares are non-refundable within 24 hours of departure except for park-initiated cancellations such as a site closure; standby seating is released ten minutes before each sailing; bicycles, kayaks and oversized gear are subject to space-available loading at the sole discretion of the vessel crew; the ferry operator is not affiliated with the campsite reservation system and cannot modify a campsite booking. Weather and safety notice: conditions on San Francisco Bay can change rapidly; small-craft advisories may be issued with little notice during the shoulder season; visitors relying on the last return sailing of the day should build in schedule margin, since a missed final sailing on an island park requires an unplanned overnight or a private water-taxi charter at substantial additional cost. [Secondary boilerplate block, also repeated on every fetch] Trail conditions addendum: the Perimeter Road remains open to foot and bicycle traffic between all ferry landings; the North Ridge Fire Road is closed to bicycles above the historic battery due to erosion control work through the end of the season; visitors are reminded that cell coverage is intermittent on the north and west sides of the island and that the ranger kiosk maintains a landline for emergencies. Historical and interpretive note: Angel Island served as an immigration station, a military garrison across three wars, and a former missile site; several campsites sit near preserved fortifications that are listed on the National Register of Historic Places, and visitors are asked not to disturb any masonry, signage, or artifacts encountered along interpretive trails near the campsites. Fee schedule addendum: the nightly campsite fee covers up to six people per site and one vehicle-equivalent of gear brought by ferry; additional gear beyond the standard allotment may incur a porter fee arranged directly with the park concessionaire; senior and disability fee reductions are available at the kiosk with valid documentation and are applied at check-in rather than at the time of the original online reservation. Reservation system note: this status endpoint reflects the same underlying inventory used by the public reservation website and by the phone reservation line; a change made through one channel is reflected in the others within a few minutes, though the public website cache may lag the authoritative inventory by up to fifteen minutes during high-traffic periods. Concessionaire notice: the camp store near Ayala Cove sells firewood, ice, and basic supplies from 9am to 4pm daily during the season, cash and card both accepted, and does not accept campsite reservation changes or refund requests, which must go through the state parks reservation system directly rather than through the concessionaire.
